source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 9 (2022), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.209
title: Independent boundary trace controllability for a disjoint heat cascade
difficulty_reason: Use unique continuation outside the observation set and weak boundary trace duality to annihilate the first boundary datum, then an energy identity to propagate vanishing through the second component. The disjoint coupling and observation geometry rules out the immediate local coupling argument.

standard_prerequisites.name: Classical heat equation and functional analysis
standard_prerequisites.statement: Weak and transposition solutions, Sobolev trace maps and parabolic regularity, Holmgren unique continuation, Hilbert-space range/kernel duality, standard heat observability and convex minimization. The displayed Hadamard derivative formula is a standard supplied input. Target-specific constructions remain in the original proof.

core_obligations: Use unique continuation outside the observation set and weak boundary trace duality to annihilate the first boundary datum, then an energy identity to propagate vanishing through the second component. The disjoint coupling and observation geometry rules out the immediate local coupling argument.

compared.difference: Public 2109 is finite-dimensional nonlinear shape desensitization (Thm-Case1-Exact-FD); this independently controls arbitrary pairs of boundary fluxes and retains the original unique-continuation argument. It is not the direct zero-flux desensitization corollary.

dedup.scope: Compared same-source public manifest item, existing heat obstruction card and the three new heat targets; no direct desensitization corollaries counted.
